scenes.narration: Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Petteri Orpo — in that order. Antti Petteri Orpo (born 3 November 1969) is a Finnish politician currently serving as the prime minister of Finland since 2023. He has also been the leader of the National Coalition Party since 2016 and briefly served as speaker of the Parliament of Finland after the 2023 parliamentary election.

The turning point in the life of Petteri Orpo looked like a failure at the time. He served as Deputy Prime Minister of Finland from 2017 to 2019, Minister of Finance from 2016 to 2019, Minister of the Interior from 2015 to 2016 and Minister of Agriculture and Forestry from 2014 to 2015. On 2 April 2023, Orpo's National Coalition Party won the 2023 parliamentary election with a plurality of 20.8% of the vote and 48 seats.

Every biography of Petteri Orpo has to pass through the years that were quietly lost. Antti Petteri Orpo was born on 3 November 1969 in Köyliö, Finland. Later Orpo earned a master's degree in political science from the University of Turku.

The education of Petteri Orpo happened mostly outside any school. Orpo attended Finland's mandatory national armed service and became a reserve officer. During his tenure as Minister of the Interior, Orpo received support for his handling of the 2015 migration crisis from coalition partners in the anti-immigration Finns Party, as well as from opposition lawmakers.

What Petteri Orpo wanted at the start and what Petteri Orpo got are not the same thing, and that gap is the story. In May 2016, Orpo announced that he would challenge the chair of the National Coalition Party and incumbent Minister of Finance Alexander Stubb in June's party conference. At the time, Orpo joined second-term parliamentarian Elina Valtonen in seeking to replace Stubb.

The defining trait of Petteri Orpo was not talent — it was the refusal to stop. In contrast to polyglot and outspoken Stubb, Orpo was widely seen as a careful consensus-seeker with little experience of international politics. Orpo received 441,4 votes against Stubb's 361 and was thus elected as the new chair for the party.

Those who met Petteri Orpo at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. Orpo soon announced that he would take Stubb's seat as the Minister of Finance. In June 2017, Prime Minister Juha Sipilä and Orpo announced said they could not cooperate with their parties' third coalition partner, the Finns Party, anymore, citing differences in core values and in the immigration and EU policies.

The private years of Petteri Orpo explain the public decades better than any speech. For both Sipilä and Orpo, at stake were major healthcare and local government reform, which were key to their plan to balance public finances. In addition to his national political roles, Orpo co-chaired (alongside Valdis Dombrovskis) the EPP Economic and Financial Affairs Ministers Meeting, which gathers the centre-right European People's Party (EPP) ministers ahead of meetings of the Economic and Financial Affairs Council (ECOFIN).

The family Petteri Orpo came from matters more than the legends admit. In December 2019 Orpo attempted a vote of no-confidence in the incumbent government. The incumbent government was accused of malpractice in responding to problems in the labor market.

The first real success of Petteri Orpo arrived later than anyone expected, and changed everything. Later, Prime Minister Antti Rinne resigned, and Kulmuni publicly refused to join the National Coalition Party's plan of premature elections. When the chairman of the Defence Committee of the Parliament Ilkka Kanerva died in the spring of 2022, the National Coalition Party parliamentary group nominated Orpo as his successor.

The last chapter of Petteri Orpo was written long after the fame. The chairman of the National Coalition Party parliamentary group Kai Mykkänen announced that the party wanted its chairman to be centrally involved in Finland's NATO process and that Orpo would act as the chairman of the committee specifically during the NATO membership process. The fact that the party chairman also served as the chairman of the committee was considered exceptional.

The whole life of Petteri Orpo reads like a single decision repeated. Orpo was elected as a member of the committee on 22 April 2022 and the committee elected him as its chairman on 26 April. Orpo told the target schedule that the NATO process would be completed by the summer, after which another National Coalition Party MP would be elected to the position.

Between the birth and the legend of Petteri Orpo lie the years that actually decide it. On September 9, 2022, Orpo stepped down as chairman of the committee and was succeeded by Antti Häkkänen. On 2 April 2023, Orpo's National Coalition Party won the 2023 Finnish parliamentary election.

The reputation of Petteri Orpo was built in the middle, not at the edges. The party had led the polls since mid-2021 and finished first, with 20.8% of the votes and 48 seats in the parliament, increasing their total by 10 seats. Orpo began government formation talks when the new parliament and President convened the week after Easter and named him as the lead negotiator.

Somebody like Petteri Orpo should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. Orpo campaigned on a platform of reducing Finland's government debt and the yearly budget deficit as well as reducing income taxes. Orpo was elected by parliamentary groups as the Speaker of the Parliament of Finland on 12 April on a temporary basis until a new government is formed.

The life of Petteri Orpo begins far from where the story usually starts. On 27 April, it was announced that Orpo would begin final negotiations with the Finns Party, the Swedish People's Party and the Christian Democrats to form a coalition government. This coalition of parties was confirmed on 15 June, with the government formation, including the names of its ministers, announced on 17 June.

Petteri Orpo was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. His party received eight cabinet posts, the Finns Party seven (including the Ministries of Finance, the Interior and Justice), while the Swedish People's Party and the Christian Democrats shared the remaining five. It is Finland's most right-wing government since the end of the Second World War; indeed, it is one of the few occasions since the return of peace that one side of the Finnish political spectrum has been able to form a government on its own.

To understand where Petteri Orpo ended up, start with where Petteri Orpo began. Petteri Orpo announced a €6 billion cut in the state budget, stating that the greatest danger threatening Finland was "the debt crisis" (it stands at 74% of GDP), and reforms, some of which "are going to hurt". For example, the conditions for receiving unemployment benefit will be tightened, a one-day waiting period will be introduced at the start of sick leave, and access to housing benefit will be restricted.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Petteri Orpo ran through years nobody filmed. In addition, the right to strike will be restricted and a fine introduced for unauthorized work stoppages. The government agreement also provides for easier redundancies and the use of fixed-term contracts, while increasing investment in vocational training.

Each stage of the life of Petteri Orpo made the next stage possible. These announcements were welcomed by employers, who see in the program the reforms they have been "demanding for decades", but the unions denounced "an attack on employees". Asylum will no longer be granted on a temporary basis, and six full years' residence in Finland will be required to apply for a permanent residence permit.

The people who knew Petteri Orpo young describe someone already restless. In addition, the country will only accept 500 refugees per year under the relocation scheme, compared with 1,050 at present. Immigrant workers will no longer have the same privileges as permanent residents, and will have to leave the country within three months of being laid off.

What Petteri Orpo built in the middle years is what the name still stands for. During the first month of his cabinet, there were numerous scandals regarding past writings by the Finns Party ministers, including the Deputy Prime Minister Riikka Purra. The scandal around Nazi-connected joking and potential connections to neo-Nazi organisations of Minister of Economic Affairs Vilhelm Junnila led to him resigning.

By the time Petteri Orpo reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. Orpo's Cabinet's party Swedish People's Party of Finland have criticized Orpo for too weak leadership during the Junnila scandal. Orpo's leadership among the various controversies was also questioned and criticized widely in Finnish and international media.

The rise of Petteri Orpo was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. In March 2024 Orpo stated in Politico that the Finns are not a far-right party anymore in his opinion. After Orpo opened an anti racist campaign of his cabinet in August 2024 Deputy Prime Minister Purra stated the Finns Party likely do not participate as a party and added "better immigration policy" as an example of her anti-racist deeds.

Setbacks came early for Petteri Orpo, and the response to them is the real story. He condemned Hamas' actions during the Gaza war and expressed his support to Israel and its right to self-defense. The Orpo cabin has approved the two-state solution as solution of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.

The legacy of Petteri Orpo outlived the circumstances that produced it. In August 2025 Orpo stated that the two-state solution will be realized when all Western and Arab countries are committed to supporting the existence of both the Palestinian and Israeli states. Although in 2019 Orpo was co-founder of Coalition of Finance Ministers for Climate Action his cabinet's Finance Minister Riikka Purra stated in January 2024 that climate matters are not responsibility of the Finance Minister.

Few lives travel as far as that of Petteri Orpo, and the distance is the point. In 2024, Orpo condemned racist attacks made against Daniela Owusu, a Finnish-Ghanaian woman who was elected to serve as Saint Lucy for the national Saint Lucy's Day celebrations, and issued a formal apology to Owusu. In December 2025, Miss Finland at the time, Sarah Dzafce, was reported to have made racist remarks on social media directed against East Asians.
